piezas.titulo: Grammar in context: Numbers, age and basic details
texto: Quantity and counting structures: unlike English («three people»), in Thai nouns are not linked directly to numbers. A numeral classifier is needed, following the pattern: [Noun] + [Number] + [Classifier]. To count people, «คน» (khon) is used: «มีคนสามคน» (There are three people). For age, «ปี» works as a time classifier: «อายุสามสิบปี» (Age: 30 years). For dates: «วันที่» + [Number]: «วันที่ห้า» (Day 5).

pregunta.texto: What is the correct syntactic order in Thai for saying «three people» when counting?

opciones.texto: คน (noun) + สาม (number) + คน (classifier)
opciones.explicacion: Correct: it follows the standard rule [Noun] + [Number] + [Classifier].
Incorrect: putting the number before the noun, as English does, is ungrammatical in standard Thai.

opciones.texto: คน + คน + สาม
opciones.explicacion: Incorrect: the number must come immediately before its classifier.
